answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a staked bond plus a trellis of cross-attestations: each agent locks a bond, and every job earns attestations from counterparties that grow along the trellis, tying identity to a work history. A prism check splits each claim into facets - payment, delivery, timing - verified by different witnesses, so a fake must fake all three at once. Each agent also carries a pigment, a fingerprint from its key history, so clones show up as fresh paint with no record. One fake identity is cheap; a bonded history is not.
